seo.title: Apple Business Actions: Add Booking and Order Buttons
seo.meta_description: How to add Actions such as Order, Reserve and Menu to your Apple Maps place card with Apple Business, requirements and approval times, for Orange County.

h1: Apple Business Actions: Add Order, Reserve and Booking Buttons to Apple Maps
answer: Apple Business Actions are buttons on your Apple Maps place card, such as Order, Menu or Reserve, that link to your website or preferred platform. Your first Action becomes the Primary Action, shown next to your website button. Apple approves Actions, which can take up to three business days. Anaheim and Orange County businesses can use them to turn Maps views into bookings and orders.
key_takeaways: Actions are buttons on the place card.
The first Action becomes the Primary Action.
Approval can take up to three business days.

sections.heading: Apple Business Connect is now Apple Business
sections.body_html: Apple's guide states that Apple Business Connect is now Apple Business, which combines what was previously in Apple Business Manager, Apple Business Essentials and Apple Business Connect into one offering. If you used Apple Business Connect before, you can sign in to Apple Business with the same personal Apple Account.

sections.heading: What Actions are
sections.body_html: Apple's guide says Actions appear on place cards by adding a direct link to your brand's website or preferred platform. Maps users access them at the top of the place card through the Primary Action or More, with names such as Order or Tickets.

sections.heading: Category Actions
sections.body_html: Each category has several Action types. Apple's restaurant example includes Menu, Reserve, Waitlist, Pickup and Delivery. You can create Actions for the ones that fit and leave others empty.

sections.heading: The Primary Action
sections.body_html: Apple says the Primary Action appears as a button to the right of your website button, and under More with other Actions. Your very first Action automatically becomes the Primary Action; you can change it later.

sections.heading: Requirements
sections.body_html:
• Customers need iOS 17.4 or iPadOS 17.4 or later to use Actions on iPhone and iPad.
  • A URL can't be used in more than one Action type.
  • A URL can't exactly match a third-party partner's Action URL.
  • Apple must approve Actions, which can take up to three business days.

sections.heading: Actions in showcases
sections.body_html: Showcases can include an Action as their call-to-action button, linking a promotion straight to ordering or booking.

sections.heading: Partner Actions
sections.body_html: Apple notes that Actions can also be created through the Apple Business Partner API, and some Actions are available only that way. Booking or ordering platforms you already use may support them.

sections.heading: Actions by business type
sections.body_html:
• Restaurants: Menu, Reserve, Pickup, Delivery.
  • Salons and spas: booking.
  • Venues: tickets.
  • Service businesses: a quote or booking page.

sections.heading: Use direct links
sections.body_html: Link each Action to the page where the customer completes that task, not your homepage. Test every link on an iPhone after approval.

sections.heading: Match your Google links
sections.body_html: Use the same booking and ordering pages you link from your Google Business Profile, so customers get the same experience wherever they find you.

sections.heading: Common mistakes
sections.body_html:
• Linking every Action to the homepage.
  • Reusing one URL for several Action types.
  • Forgetting to test on an iPhone.
  • Leaving an old provider's link in place.
  • Not choosing the right Primary Action.

sections.heading: Questions owners ask us
sections.body_html: Owners often ask which Action should be primary. Choose the action most customers take: Order for a takeout restaurant, Reserve for a sit-down restaurant, booking for a salon or clinic. Another common question is why an Action doesn't appear. It may still be in review, which can take up to three business days, or the customer's device may be on an older iOS version. Owners also ask whether Actions replace a phone number. They don't; many customers still call, so keep your phone number accurate and answered. Actions simply give people who prefer to book or order online a faster route from Apple Maps to your business.

sections.heading: Checklist
sections.body_html:
• Action types chosen for your category.
  • Each Action links to a specific page.
  • Primary Action chosen.
  • Approved by Apple.
  • Tested on an iPhone.
  • Same links as Google.

sections.heading: An example
sections.body_html: Imagine a sushi restaurant in Irvine that takes reservations and pickup orders. It adds a Reserve Action linking to its booking page and a Pickup Action linking to its ordering page, making Reserve the Primary Action. After approval, iPhone users who find the restaurant in Maps can book a table in two taps.

sections.heading: How this fits your local plan
sections.body_html: It helps to see where this sits in the bigger picture. Google ranks local results mainly on relevance, distance and popularity, and AI assistants lean on the same public information: your Business Profile, your website, other listings and what customers write. For a business in Anaheim or anywhere in Orange County, the most reliable plan is simple and repeated: keep every listing accurate, explain each service clearly on its own page, show real proof of your work and reply to customers. Small improvements here compound, and they are far harder for competitors to copy than an ad budget.

sections.heading: What to do this week
sections.body_html:
1. List the actions customers take.
  2. Add matching Actions.
  3. Choose the Primary Action.
  4. Test each link after approval.

sections.heading: When to get help
sections.body_html: Plenty of owners handle this themselves. Outside help pays off when time is short, when the business has many locations or when a problem is costing calls every day it stays unresolved. Be wary of anyone who promises guaranteed positions or asks for your verification codes or passwords; Google says nobody can pay for a better local ranking. Look for clear explanations, honest timelines and reporting tied to real enquiries. Chimera offers exactly that to businesses in Anaheim and across Orange County.

sections.heading: Matching Actions to your category
sections.body_html: Think about the one thing most customers want to do after finding you. A taqueria with lots of takeout wants Order or Pickup first; a sit-down restaurant wants Reserve; a salon, spa or clinic wants booking; a venue wants Tickets. Make that the Primary Action, then add secondary Actions such as Menu or Delivery under More. Check that each linked page works on a phone, loads quickly and lets customers finish the task without hunting. Review Actions whenever you change booking or ordering providers, because an old link left in place sends customers to a dead end and makes Apple Maps look broken. Compare Action taps in Apple Business insights month to month to see which ones customers actually use. If an Action gets few taps, check whether the linked page is slow or confusing on a phone before removing it, and ask a friend to try booking or ordering from Apple Maps while you watch.

sections.heading: The short version
sections.body_html: Add Actions for the tasks customers want, link each to the right page, choose a sensible Primary Action and test on an iPhone. Chimera, based in Anaheim, sets up Apple and Google action links together for Orange County businesses.

faqs.a: Buttons on your Apple Maps place card, such as Order or Reserve, linking to your website or platform.

faqs.q: Which Action is the Primary Action?
faqs.a: Your first Action by default; you can change it.

faqs.q: How long does Action approval take?
What iOS version do customers need?
Can I use the same URL for two Actions?
faqs.a: No. Apple says a URL can't appear in more than one Action type.
Some Actions are available through the Apple Business Partner API.
